text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--In an interview ahead of President Bill Clinton's visit to Denmark on July 10 & 11, U.S. Copenhagen ambassador Edward Elson pours accolades on Danes for their leading role in the fight for democracy and liberty, dubbing Denmark America's best friend in Europe.

--Opposition Conservative leader Per Stig Moeller predicted that the autumn negotiations with the Social Democrat-led minority coalition on 1998's state budget would not end in premature elections. Moeller said his party would aim at reaching agreement on education and the health service finances with the government.
--FDB - Denmark's biggest supermarket chain - plans to go international and diversify into non-food activity, with Nordic cooperation with Swedish and Norwegian groups as a first step.

--Confederation of Danish Industry director Hans Skov Christensen openly calls for Danish participation in EMU regardless of the consequences. Christensen's call conflicts with economic wisemen's warnings in a recent report that Denmark should stay outside European economic and monetary cooperation until it was certain that the new euro single currency was strong.

--A broad majority in the Danish parliament gave prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen and foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen a mandate to negotiate a deal for Denmark at the EU Amsterdam summit, maintaining the country's opt-outs on EMU, joint defence, EU citizenship and police and legal cooperation.
